approach: Let `athena retry <stale job>` through, then give the new job a path that never calls the producer when it does not need one. (1) `earlier_attempt_with` (reading.rs) accepts `Closed(Stale)`, carries the stale reason, and the reader brief says the job "went stale" instead of "was rejected" or "starts from the base". (2) In `dispatch` (run/mod.rs) a new `stale_seed` looks at the retried job's records. It needs a stale job with a candidate that has no violations, a passing verification whose fingerprint still matches, and both commits still in the repository. It then merges the old candidate onto the branch tip with a new `Git::merge_tree_conflicts` (athena-git lib.rs; git `merge-tree --write-tree --name-only`). (3) Clean merge: the existing `resume_candidate` runs with a `stale` flag. It re-merges on the new job's prediction commit, builds the candidate commit, runs admission, then `check_and_verify` (checks, replay, verifier). It returns before any planner or producer runs. Landing is the normal `land_or_block`, so `plan()` in land.rs still asserts fingerprint(landed tree) == verified fingerprint. (4) Conflict: the conflicted merge tree (markers kept) seeds the producer's work tree through the existing `SnapshotRepo::BaseThenTree`. A new `RetrySeed.conflicts` field makes the producer brief explain the stale conflict. The producer's result is checked and verified in full, so nothing lands without a new verification. (5) Docs: the reversal of D10 alternative (d) is appended as D157 and no existing line is edited. The wording avoids the phrases `supersedes`, `superseded by` and `amends`, because the real-log backtest test counts those hits against decision-links.toml, which is out of scope. CHANGELOG, README, retry help and the stale outcome reason (close.rs) are updated. The staleness rules in land.rs `plan()` are not changed.

decisions.choice: Merge with git three-way `merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<old base> <new base> <old candidate>` on the new job's prediction commit, instead of re-applying the candidate's diff on top of the new base.
decisions.reason: The existing resume overlay (`resume_candidate`, run/mod.rs ~572) puts the candidate's files over the base. If the tip changed the same file, that would silently drop the tip's change. A real merge keeps both sides and reports a conflict, which is the case the brief needs to detect. `Git::merge_tree` already does this for landing replay (land.rs:117), so the merge semantics match what landing already trusts.

rejected.option: Overlay the old candidate's changed files on the tip (reuse the resume overlay unchanged).
rejected.why: Overwrites tip changes in any file both sides touched, with no conflict signal.
`qualifies_for_tree_retry` requires state Rejected, and `tree_seed` refuses any change outside records/, which is exactly the stale case.

decisions.choice: Do the merge twice: a preflight against `head` in `dispatch` (to choose clean vs conflict path and build the conflict seed), and the authoritative merge against the prediction commit inside `resume_candidate`.
decisions.reason: The candidate commit must sit on the prediction commit `p`, and its tree must contain the new job's own records files, or the landing tree would drop them. The prediction commit differs from `head` only under records/, which the candidate never touches, so the preflight and the real merge agree. If they ever disagree, `resume_candidate` closes the job failed with a reason and lands nothing.

rejected.option: Merge only against `head` and commit that tree on `p`.
rejected.why: The tree would lack the job's dispatch records; landing would delete them.

rejected.option: Merge only inside `resume_candidate` and fall back to the producer from there.
rejected.why: The producer path is chosen earlier in `dispatch`; moving it would restructure the dispatch flow.

decisions.choice: For a conflict, seed the producer's work tree with the conflicted merge tree (tip files plus the candidate's changes, conflict markers in the conflicted files) and add `RetrySeed.conflicts: Option<Vec<String>>` so the brief names the stale job and the conflicting paths.
decisions.reason: It keeps the tip's other work in the producer's directory, which `BaseThenTree` seeding from the old candidate alone would revert. It also gives the producer both sides of each conflict. The new candidate is built from the work tree against the base and goes through admission, checks and the verifier like any producer result.

rejected.option: Start the conflict retry from the base with the old candidate described only in prose.
rejected.why: The producer's snapshot has no other branches or history, so it could not see the kept candidate's content; the brief asks for a retry seeded from it.

rejected.option: Seed with the old candidate's tree via BaseThenTree.
rejected.why: It undoes the tip's work in the work tree; the guard in `tree_seed` exists to prevent that.
Its fixed text says the producer reached its deadline, which would be false.

decisions.choice: Gate the stale path on records, not prose: the retried job's state is `Closed(Stale)`, its candidate has a commit and no violations, `Verified::from_record` accepts its verification (verdict pass and recorded fingerprint equal to a fresh `fingerprint(candidate, base)`), and both commits resolve. Anything else retries from the base as today.
decisions.reason: A candidate whose verification no longer matches its content must not be treated as verified. Falling back keeps the existing behavior for odd records (commits garbage-collected, an unverified job).

rejected.option: Trust any stale job's candidate record.
rejected.why: `Verified::from_record` is the existing check that the verified content is the candidate content.

risks.risk: A textually clean merge can be semantically wrong (the tip changed an API the candidate uses); re-verification is the only guard.
risks.mitigation: Run the checks, replay and verifier on the merged tree, since the merge is a new tree. The clean path calls `check_and_verify` unchanged, so a bad merge fails a check or the verifier. Landing still bails if landed != verified.

risks.risk: A producer that changes nothing in a conflicted work tree would be passed on with conflict markers still in it (existing `unchanged_since_seed` behavior).
risks.mitigation: The brief tells the producer which files conflict and to resolve every marker. Admission and the checks run on the producer's result in the usual way, so a candidate with markers fails the checks or the verifier. The unchanged-since-seed path of `BaseThenTree` is the existing behavior for seeded retries; the test asserts the verifier runs.

risks.risk: A stale job whose verification record is missing or whose commits were removed would otherwise get a broken seed.
risks.mitigation: `stale_seed` returns None unless `Verified::from_record` accepts the verification with a freshly computed fingerprint and both commits resolve. Otherwise dispatch runs the existing retry-from-base path.

risks.risk: The preflight merge (against head) and the real merge (against the prediction commit) could differ.
risks.mitigation: Merge on `head` for the preflight and again on the prediction commit inside `resume_candidate`. If the second merge conflicts anyway, the job closes failed with a reason and lands nothing.

risks.risk: Refactoring `resume_candidate` could change the existing environment-stop resume.
risks.mitigation: Keep `stale = false` on the existing paths, so the overlay code runs exactly as before. The three existing resume tests in run/tests.rs cover it.

risks.risk: The new decision text creates an unlisted supersession hit and fails `the_real_log_has_no_condition_a_finding_against_the_confirmed_list`.
risks.mitigation: Keep D157 free of those three phrases; the real-log backtest test and the decisions test are in the criterion 5 and 6 demonstrations.
The existing merge-tree call in athena-git already needs `--write-tree`, which arrived in the same git release (2.38) as `--name-only`, so no new minimum version is introduced.

risks.risk: Leaving display.rs:840 unchanged leaves a hint that does not mention retry.
risks.mitigation: Raised as a user question; the outcome reason in close.rs carries the pointer meanwhile.

demonstrations.method: Integration test in crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs, beside `a_governed_change_on_the_branch_makes_the_job_stale` (line 2027). Run a job so a user commit lands on the branch during verification and the job ends `Stale`. Then call `Athena::retry(job, &Lines::default())`.
demonstrations.observes: `retry` returns Ok with a Proposal whose `reading` is Some. The retry's request record is `try again on <job>`. The stale job is left unchanged. A queued job is still refused with the old message prefix (retry.rs:393 unchanged).
demonstrations.fails_without: `earlier_attempt_with` (reading.rs:1362-1374) bails with `job … is stale; only a rejected or failed job can be tried again`, so `Athena::retry` returns Err and the `unwrap` in the test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::retry`. Fixture: `Fixture`, `Scenario.during_verification` (tests/common/mod.rs:428) and the fake agent driver, injected through `fx.athena(scenario.script())`. All exist today; the test is new (step 14). The tip commit changes `src/lib.rs` and the candidate only README.md, so the later merge is clean.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs next to `interrupted_job_with_a_candidate_resumes_without_planner_or_producer` (line 3762). Wrap `counting(...)` so the first verifier turn commits `OTHER.md` on the branch (the job goes Stale), then `retry` the job and `go` the retry job with a `Lines` ui.
demonstrations.observes: After the first go the counts are (planner 0, producer 1, verifier 1) and the outcome is Stale. After retry and go: the producer count is still 1 and the verifier count is 2. The ui lines include `resume     `, `checks     ` and `replay     `, and the state is Landed. README.md at HEAD contains the demo text and `OTHER.md` is kept. The retry's candidate record has `base_commit` equal to the new tip's prediction commit.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the stale path in `dispatch`/`resume_candidate`, either `retry` errors (criterion 1), or the retry job runs the producer, so the producer count rises from 1 to 2 and the asserts on `(planner, producer, …)` fail. If the merged tree skipped the checks, the `checks     ` and `replay     ` lines would be missing. If it skipped verification, the verifier count would stay 1.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `Athena::retry` and `Athena::go`, which reach `dispatch`, `stale_seed` and `resume_candidate`. Counting double: `Counts` and `counting()` (run/tests.rs:2119, 2152), `repo()`, `athena_with()`, `Lines` all exist. The tip-moving wrapper script is new in step 13. It only runs `git commit`; the merge and verification logic stay in production code.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs. The tip commit rewrites the same README.md line the candidate changed, so the job goes Stale. After `retry`, check the repository head is unchanged by the retry command, then `go` the retry job.
demonstrations.observes: A second producer run happens, so the producer count is 2. That run's work directory README.md contains `<<<<<<<` and the kept candidate's text. Its producer brief contains the conflict section and names the stale job. The verifier runs again (count 2) before any landing. The state is Landed with a Verification record whose `verified_fingerprint` equals the fingerprint of the landed commit.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the conflict branch the retry either lands the overlaid candidate, losing the tip's README change, or fails. The asserts that the producer ran a second time, saw markers in a README seeded from the candidate, and that the verifier count rose before the landing, would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `Athena::retry` and `Athena::go`. Double: the same `counting()` wrapper, extended to record the producer's `spec.workdir` README and `spec.user_prompt` (the pattern is `two_phases` in tests/retry.rs:525). It is injected through `athena_with(... script)`. Existing: `Counts`, `athena_with`. New in step 13: the recording wrapper and the tip-moving commit.

demonstrations.method: land.rs unit test with the existing `repo()`, `commit()` and `pass()` fixtures. Move the tip, build a candidate commit on the tip from `Git::merge_tree_conflicts`, then call `plan`. The core test above also asserts the end-to-end equality. `land::tests` runs the existing `Plan::Stale` tests (`a_base_that_is_no_longer_an_ancestor…`, `a_changed_exclusion_rule…`) unchanged.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core --lib a_merged_candidate_lands_content_with_the_verified_fingerprint && cargo test -p athena-core --lib a_stale_job_whose_candidate_merges_cleanly && cargo test -p athena-core --lib land::tests
demonstrations.observes: `plan(...)` returns `Plan::Tree(t)` with `fingerprint(t, base) == verified.fingerprint()`. The same call with a different fingerprint returns Err. In the core test the retry's `verification.verified_fingerprint` equals `fingerprint(git, landed_commit, retry_base)`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the landed tree did not match the verified merged tree, `plan()` would bail with `the content to land … differs from the verified content` and the equality assert would fail. If the wrong-fingerprint case no longer errored, `landing_refuses_content_that_differs_from_the_verified_content` and the new refusal assert would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `land::plan`; `Git::merge_tree_conflicts` is new (step 3). Fixtures `base_and_candidate`, `pass`, `commit` exist in land.rs tests (used at lines 590-611, 706-709). Nothing is faked: real git repositories in temp dirs.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks. The decisions test lives in crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs:253.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0. The decisions test passes with `PINNED_LEN` and `PINNED_SHA256` untouched, because D157 is appended after the pinned prefix and has a Provenance bullet.
demonstrations.fails_without: A formatting or lint slip, an edit to a pinned decision line (`the_decision_log_is_well_formed_and_only_appended_to` would report `the first 230046 bytes changed`), or a D157 hit not listed in the links file (the real-log backtest test) would fail the run.
demonstrations.seam: Not applicable; it runs the whole workspace. No test double is involved.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of docs/decisions.md and Grep for `## D157` and `Automatic re-verification on the new base`. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --lib the_decision_log_is_well_formed_and_only_appended_to` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test backtest the_real_log_has_no_condition_a_finding_against_the_confirmed_list`.
demonstrations.observes: The diff has only `+` lines, all after D156. The new entry D157 states it reverses the left-out alternative (d) 'Automatic re-verification on the new base' of the landing decision D10 (cited by id), and gives the reason that stale landings now recur with parallel jobs. It has no `supersedes`, `superseded by` or `amends` phrase.
demonstrations.fails_without: An edit to D10 (line 297) would show as a removed `-` line and would also fail `the_decision_log_is_well_formed_and_only_appended_to`.
demonstrations.seam: Not a behavior criterion; there is no double. Existing test files read the real docs/decisions.md and docs/decision-links.toml.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff. Grep CHANGELOG.md for `stale` under `## [Unreleased]` and README.md lines 48-63.
demonstrations.observes: CHANGELOG has one new entry under Unreleased/Added that says only what the diff does. Retry accepts a stale job and merges its kept candidate onto the tip. A clean merge is checked, replayed, re-verified and landed with no producer run. A conflict runs the producer from the candidate, and nothing lands without a new verification. It names the root cause and D157. README no longer lists stale among the refused states and describes the stale retry.
demonstrations.fails_without: If README.md still said stale jobs are refused, the old sentence at README.md lines 57-58 (`Jobs that are landed, stale, in flight, or unknown are refused`) would remain in the diff context unchanged.
demonstrations.seam: Not a behavior criterion; there is no double.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests plus one CLI test. The briefs.rs test builds `EarlierAttempt { end_state: "stale", .. }` and calls `reader_brief`. The reading.rs test replaces Stale in `only_rejected_or_failed_jobs_can_be_tried_again` (line 4653) with a test that `earlier_attempt` accepts a stale job and carries its reason. The CLI test runs `athena retry --help`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-context reader_briefs_say_a_stale_earlier_attempt_went_stale && cargo test -p athena-core --lib a_stale_job_can_be_tried_again && cargo test -p athena-cli --test retry the_retry_command_help_covers_stale_jobs
demonstrations.observes: The brief contains `went stale` and says the kept candidate is merged onto the tip. It does not contain `was rejected` or `A retry starts from the base` unqualified for a stale job. The help text names stale jobs and the merge behavior.
demonstrations.fails_without: The brief would still say `which was rejected` and `A retry starts from the base` for a stale job, so the new brief asserts fail. The help text would still start `Try a rejected or failed job again`, so the help assert fails.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `reader_brief`, `earlier_attempt` and the binary `CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena`. Double: none for the briefs and the reading; the CLI test runs the real binary like `the_retry_command_takes_a_job_and_the_same_options_as_ask` (retry.rs:874). Fixtures `job_with_checks`, `records_with` and `outcome` exist in reading.rs tests; the new tests are added in steps 6 and 10.

demonstrations.method: Run `git status` and `git diff --stat`, then Grep the diff for secrets and email-like text. The boundary scan (`xtask` policy test) runs inside `cargo test --locked`.
demonstrations.observes: Only the 13 listed files are modified. No new files. No secrets, no email-like text, no banned words.
demonstrations.fails_without: A file outside the list (for example display.rs or decision-links.toml) would appear in the status output.
demonstrations.seam: Not a behavior criterion; there is no double.

open_questions: User: crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs:840 still tells the user to 'ask again' after a stale job, and the file is not a listed deliverable. Should a follow-up change point that hint at `athena retry <job>`? This plan covers the hint only through the outcome reason in close.rs.

User: should docs/decision-links.toml get a [[link]] marking D10 as amended by D157? The brief puts that file out of scope, so D157 avoids the phrases the backtest parser counts; the decision view will then show D10 as unamended.

Host: the stale path assumes the old candidate commit object is still in the repository (candidate commits are unreferenced objects). Whether the host's git garbage collection removes them before a user retries cannot be read from the code; the plan falls back to the old retry-from-base behavior when `rev_parse` finds no commit.
